summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of primary sclerosing cholangitis, cirrhosis, and recent cholangitis presented with fever, rigors, and worsening right upper quadrant abdominal pain shortly after completing a course of ertapenem. She was admitted for suspected recurrent cholangitis. Blood cultures and stool testing were negative, and imaging showed no biliary obstruction. An ERCP confirmed findings consistent with known PSC without new strictures or stones. She was treated with IV meropenem and transitioned to outpatient ertapenem via a newly placed PICC line for a two-week course. Prophylactic moxifloxacin was initiated upon discharge to reduce recurrence risk. Diuretics were held during acute infection and restarted before discharge. She improved clinically with resolution of fever and pain, and was discharged home with home health support for IV antibiotics and plans for follow-up with infectious disease, repeat endoscopy, and liver transplant evaluation.
